1.w: And the word came of YHWH to me, saying:

2.w: “And you, son of man, take up concerning Tyre a lamentation,

3.w: and to Tyre, the one dwelling at the entrances of the sea, being merchant of the peoples on many coasts, say, thus says the Lord YHWH: O Tyre, you have said: ‘I [am] perfect in beauty.’

4.w: In the midst of the seas [are] your borders, [and] your builders have perfected your beauty.

5.w: With cypress from Senir they have built for you all [your] planks; a cedar from Lebanon they took to make a mast for you.

6.w: Of oaks from Bashan they made your oars; your boards they have made with ivory, of the daughter of the Ashurites from the coasts of Kittim.

7.w: Of fine linen with embroidery from Egypt was your sail, to be for you a banner; blue and purple from the coasts of Elishah was your awning.

8.w: Those dwelling in Sidon and Arvad were the rowers for you; your wise men, O Tyre, were in you—they [were] your pilots.

9.w: Elders of Gebal and her wise men were in you, strengthening your breaches; all the ships of the sea and their sailors were in you, to offer merchandise to you.

10.w: Persia and Lydia and Libya were in your force, as men of war for you; shield and helmet they hung within you—they gave splendor to you.

11.w: The sons of Arvad and Helech [were] on your walls round about, and the Gammadites were on your towers; their shields they hung on your walls round about—they perfected your beauty.

12.w: Tarshish [was] your merchant, from the abundance of all wealth—in silver, iron, tin, and lead—they gave [for] your wares.

13.w: Javan, Tubal, and Meshech, they traded in souls of man and vessels of bronze—they gave [for] your merchandise.

14.w: From the house of Togarmah, horses and steeds and mules they gave [for] your wares.

15.w: The sons of Dedan were your traders, many coastlands [were] your market of your hand; horns of ivory and ebony they returned as your payment.

16.w: Aram [was] your merchant, from the abundance of your works in turquoise, purple, and embroidery, and fine linen, and corals, and rubies—they gave [for] your wares.

17.w: Judah and the land of Israel they traded with you in wheat of Minnith, and meal, and honey, and oil, and balm—they gave [for] your merchandise.

18.w: Damascus traded with you for the abundance of your works, from the abundance of all [your] wealth—with wine of Helbon and with wool of Sahar.

19.w: And casks of wine from Izal they gave for your wares; smoothed iron, cassia, and cane were among your merchandise.

20.w: Dedan was your merchant in saddlecloths for riding.

21.w: Arabia and all the princes of Kedar, they [were] trading with you in lambs, and rams, and goats—in these they were your merchants.

22.w: The traders of Sheba and Raamah, they traded with you in the choicest of all spice, and in every of precious stone, and gold—they gave [for] your wares.

23.w: Haran, and Canneh, and Eden, were traders of Sheba, Assyria, [and] Chilmad traded with you;

24.w: they traded with you—in fine, garments of blue, embroidered work, rugs and multicolored, with cords tightly twisted and knotted—for your marketplace.

25.w: The ships of Tarshish were the transporters of your merchandise, and you were full and very heavy in the midst of the seas.

26.w: Into many waters they have brought you, those rowing for you; a wind from the east has broken you in the midst of the seas.

27.w: Your riches, and your wares, your merchandise, your mariners, and your pilots, the repairers of your breach[es], and those offering your merchandise, and all [your] men of war who [are] in you, and all your assembled [force] which [is] in your midst, will fall into the midst of the seas on the day of your downfall!

28.w: At the sound of the cry of your sailors the common lands will shake,

29.w: and they will come down from their ships—all those handling the oar, the mariners [and] all the sailors of the sea will stand at the shore.

30.w: And they will make heard over you their voice, and they will cry out bitterly, and they will bring up dust upon their heads; they will roll about in ashes.

31.w: And they will shave themselves bald because of you, and they will gird themselves with sackcloth and weep for you with bitterness of heart—bitter wailing.

32.w: And they will lift up a lamentation for you in their wailing, and they will lament over you: ‘Who [was] like Tyre, silenced in the midst of the sea?

33.w: In the going forth of your wares from the sea, you satisfied many people; with the abundance of your wealth and your merchandise, you enriched the kings of the earth.

34.w: In time [you] are broken by the seas, in the depths of the waters; your merchandise and all your assembly have fallen in your midst.

35.w: All those dwelling in the coasts are appalled over you, and their kings bristle [with] bristling; the faces trembled.

36.w: The traders among the nations hiss at you; you have become a horror, and you will be no more, even to forever!’”
